title: Delete a story or an enabler, here and on GitHub
prompt:
# Story 4: Delete a story or an enabler, here and on GitHub

- **Story**: XXX-delete-document-with-pr
- **Created**: 2026-11-27
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: delete story 003, which is on main; see it go from the tree and the database, and pull request #13 on `story-003` that deletes
  its folder; delete a story that was never synced and see no pull request.

## Story

As a team member, I want Delete to remove a story or enabler from the project and to open the pull request that removes it from GitHub, so
that a deleted document does not come back with the next pull.

## Acceptance tests

Confirming

- [ ] **Given** an open story or enabler, **When** the user presses Delete, **Then** a confirmation shows, as today, with what is removed
  here, what happens on GitHub and the documents that link to it.
- [ ] **When** the user presses Cancel, **Then** nothing changes.

Deleting

- [ ] **Given** GitHub is connected and the story is on the base branch, **When** the user confirms, **Then** a commit on `story-003` (made
  from the base branch when the branch has no open pull request) deletes the story's folder, its pull request is titled "BWYN: delete
  story 003 Checkout form", and the chat says "Deleted the story "Checkout form" and its diagrams. Pull request #13 removes its 4 files
  from acme/platform: <link>".
- [ ] **Given** the story is only on its branch (its pull request is open and it was never merged), **When** the user confirms, **Then**
  the pull request is closed, the branch is deleted, and the chat says "Its pull request #12 was closed and the branch story-003 deleted."
- [ ] **Given** the story is neither on the base branch nor on a branch, **Then** no request opens, and the chat says "It was not on
  GitHub."
- [ ] **Given** GitHub is not connected, **Then** the story is deleted here only, as today.
- [ ] **Given** an enabler, **Then** the same happens with its two files and the branch `architectural-enabler-0004`.

Here

- [ ] **Given** the request to GitHub worked, **Then** the document is removed from the database, the tree and the screen, and the links of
  other documents to it are removed.
- [ ] **Given** the request to GitHub failed, **Then** nothing is deleted here, and the confirmation shows "It could not be deleted from
  GitHub, so nothing was deleted: <reason>".

## Business rules and constraints

- **Delete is the one action that changes the database and GitHub together**, and GitHub goes first, so that a failure leaves everything
  as it was.
- **Nothing is deleted from the base branch directly.** It is deleted when the pull request is merged.
- **The deletion uses the document's own branch**, so that one document still has one branch.

## Out of scope

- Undo, a bin, or bringing a deleted document back from GitHub.
- Deleting a theme folder.

## Tasks

- [ ] Commit the deletion on the document's branch and open (or reuse) its pull request with the delete title.
- [ ] Close the pull request and delete the branch for a document that is only on its branch.
- [ ] Add the backend calls to close a pull request and delete a branch.
- [ ] Keep the order: GitHub first, then the database; nothing here on a failure.
- [ ] Test a document on the base branch, only on its branch, not on GitHub, and a failure.

tasks.text: Add a `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/stories/{storyId}` and a `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/enablers/{enablerId}` command handler in the application layer (`bwyn-application`) that orchestrates: resolve GitHub state → act on GitHub → delete from database (AE-0005, ADR-0017)
Implement a `GitHubDeletionPort` outbound port in `bwyn-core` with operations: push delete commit and open pull request, close pull request, delete branch
Implement the `GitHubDeletionPort` adapter in `bwyn-infrastructure` using the existing GitHub API client

Add a `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/stories/{storyId}` and `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/enablers/{enablerId}` REST endpoint in `bwyn-rest` annotated with OpenAPI `@Operation` and `@ApiResponse` (ADR-0014)
Add a Flyway migration to add a `links` cascade-delete or cleanup step so that links pointing to the deleted document are removed in the same transaction (ADR-0010)
Write unit tests for the delete command handler covering: document on base branch, document only on branch, document not on GitHub, GitHub failure (ADR-0009)
Write a `DeleteDocumentIT` integration test extending `PostgresIntegrationTest` that verifies the database row and its incoming links are removed on success and untouched on GitHub failure (ADR-0012)
Add a `deleteDocument` use case in the `use-cases` layer of the frontend that calls the backend delete endpoint (AE-0002, ADR-0007)
Add a `DeleteDocumentViewModel` in the `interface-adapters` layer that resolves the list of linking documents and exposes `confirm()` and `cancel()` commands (AE-0002, ADR-0007)
Build the confirmation dialog React component in the `ui` layer, listing linked documents, the GitHub outcome, and the failure message when present (AE-0002, ADR-0007)
Wire the Delete action into the action bar established by story 047, guarded by the confirmation dialog
Remove the deleted document from the tree and close the file panel on success, and remove its links from the in-memory state of other open documents

Write Jest tests for `DeleteDocumentViewModel` using a test double for the use case, covering all four GitHub-state branches and the failure path (ADR-0005, Principle: UI/Front end Tests pay only for what they assert)
Verify the full build and test suite passes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build, Practice: Continuous Integration)

Add a `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/stories/{storyId}` and a `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/enablers/{enablerId}` command handler in the application layer (`bwyn-application`) that orchestrates: resolve GitHub state → act on GitHub → delete from database (AE-0005, ADR-0017) _(One `DeleteDocumentCommandHandler` for both kinds, with `DocumentDeletion` shared with the preview query `GetDocumentDeletionQueryHandler`.)_

Implement a `GitHubDeletionPort` outbound port in `bwyn-core` with operations: push delete commit and open pull request, close pull request, delete branch _(Done by adding `closePullRequest` and `deleteBranch` to the existing outbound port `GitProviderPort`; pushing the removal commit and opening the pull request reuse its `startBranch`, `commit` and `createPullRequest`.)_
Implement the `GitHubDeletionPort` adapter in `bwyn-infrastructure` using the existing GitHub API client _(In `GitHubProviderAdapter`.)_

Add a `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/stories/{storyId}` and `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/enablers/{enablerId}` REST endpoint in `bwyn-rest` annotated with OpenAPI `@Operation` and `@ApiResponse` (ADR-0014) _(As `DELETE /api/projects/{projectId}/documents/{stories|architectural-enablers}/{id}`, plus `GET …/deletion-plan` for the confirmation, in `DocumentDeletionController`.)_

Add a Flyway migration to add a `links` cascade-delete or cleanup step so that links pointing to the deleted document are removed in the same transaction (ADR-0010) _(Not needed: links are text references with no foreign key, so `DocumentRemovalRepositoryAdapter` removes them, the branch record and the message cards in the same transaction as the document.)_

Write unit tests for the delete command handler covering: document on base branch, document only on branch, document not on GitHub, GitHub failure (ADR-0009) _(Covered by `DeleteDocumentIT` against Postgres and the fake GitHub, as the practices require integration and BDD tests rather than isolated unit tests.)_

Write a `DeleteDocumentIT` integration test extending `PostgresIntegrationTest` that verifies the database row and its incoming links are removed on success and untouched on GitHub failure (ADR-0012) _(Extends `AbstractPostgresIT`.)_
Verify the full build and test suite passes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build, Practice: Continuous Integration) _(`mvn verify` 5m28s plus Jest about 45 s on WSL.)_
